note: Curated, human-reviewed observations. Derived flags are appended by tools/flags.py on every build. Every item states what was actually checked and, where it could not be re-checked, says so instead of asserting it.

flags.item: Pinnacle publishes each LoL series twice and the pick engine was using the (Kills) derivative
flags.detail: Pinnacle's guest API lists a series moneyline plus a parallel '(Kills)' market (e.g. 'Gen.G (Kills)' vs 'Invictus (Kills)'). In the 2026-10-23T11:42Z snapshot six of eight Worlds picks were taken from the (Kills) market: Gen.G vs Invictus Gaming carried 1.282/3.740 from matchup 1638758865 while the series market 1638748200 was 1.259/3.940. A kills derivative is not a series-winner price. Fixed in this build: tools/collect.py and tools/model.py now reject any participant name containing '(Kills)' or parentId derivatives, 8 derivative markets were excluded, and the 9 remaining market picks are all true series moneylines.
flags.verification: verified live 2026-10-23 (both matchup ids visible in one Pinnacle response)

flags.item: Archived 'Esportsbook' quote was unverifiable and is replaced by live Unibet/Kambi JSON feed
flags.detail: The 0.10-weight 'Esportsbook' venue previously read static quotes from archive/session-8336fb7e/data/book_receipts.json (observed 2026-10-21T20:36Z) labelled 'EGamersWorld / GG.BET Bookmaker Feed' with a generic https://egamersworld.com/lol/matches URL. EGamersWorld returns HTTP 403 to the build runner, and its live match page for Ground Zero Gaming vs Frank Esports (LCP 2027 Promotion) renders a symmetric 1.8 / 1.8 placeholder - not the archived 1.02 / 10.5. All archived quotes remain excluded in data/retired_quotes.json (#1081423 carries an originated line), while the 0.10 slot now consumes Unibet's live public Kambi JSON feed (eu-offering-api.kambicdn.com ubse) across all 8 Worlds series for a verified 5-venue consensus (Pinnacle, Polymarket, Kalshi, Bovada, Unibet).
flags.verification: verified live 2026-10-23 (EGamersWorld shows 1.8/1.8; Unibet/Kambi ubse JSON returns 8/8 Worlds moneylines)

flags.item: Komplettligaen removed Solid Gaming in Round 10 - four Hotspawn cards cannot be priced competitively
flags.detail: Leaguepedia's Data:Komplettligaen/2026 Season/Autumn Split records the Round 10 fixture with the footnote '[[Solid Gaming]] is removed from the league.' and grades every remaining Solid Gaming series 0-2 with ff=1/ff=2 (Rounds 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 9, 10 and 11). Hotspawn still lists four of those cards as scheduled - #1071170, #1071200, #1071186 and #1071206 - and its crowd had picked the removed team on some of them. No win probability is published; instead each card carries an explicit 'official forfeit' resolution naming the opponent, valid only if Hotspawn grades the card as a walkover rather than voiding it. An earlier version of this flag cited the page Komplettligaen/2026 Season/Autumn Season, which does not exist on Leaguepedia.
flags.verification: verified live 2026-10-23 from the page wikitext (action=raw)

flags.item: Hotspawn inventory drifts between builds (264 rows on 2026-10-21, 241 rows on 2026-10-23)
flags.detail: The fixtures API only returns status=scheduled cards, so completed or delisted fixtures drop out between refreshes and the totals on this site are a point-in-time snapshot, not a fixed universe. Earlier curated notes that referenced #1071216 (Solid Gaming vs DMG Esports Norway) or a 264-match total are therefore labelled historical. Every published probability is recomputed from the current snapshot only.

flags.item: Fixture 1081423: a live external moneyline contradicts the published pick by 66.3 percentage points
flags.detail: Ground Zero Gaming vs Frank Esports (LCP 2027 Promotion, 2026-11-11 09:00Z) is published as Frank Esports 75.2% / Ground Zero Gaming 24.8% from our Elo line (Ground Zero Gaming 1511 vs Frank Esports 1703). Read on 2026-10-24T16:28Z, EGamersWorld publishes 1.025 / 10.50 for the same card, which de-vigs to Ground Zero Gaming 91.1% / Frank Esports 8.9% - a 66.3 pp gap and the opposite side. Two things make the external line credible: (1) this repository archived the identical 1.025/10.50 price on 2026-10-21 and then retired it as unverifiable because the page was showing symmetric 1.80/1.80 placeholders on 2026-10-23 - today's read shows the placeholder was a transient page state, so the retirement reason no longer holds; (2) an existing curated flag already records that Leaguepedia's Frank Esports rating may aggregate a cross-division PCS/LDL roster rather than the LCP promotion team, which is exactly the error that would inflate Frank Esports to 1703. The pick is left as published - a corroboration receipt is not an input to the model - but it should be treated as contested until the roster question is settled. The gap is reported by tools/corroborate.py on coverage.html as a divergence.
flags.verification: captured verbatim 2026-10-24T16:28Z into data/receipts/external_odds/2026-10-24-longtail.json; Hotspawn kick-off 2026-11-11T09:00:00Z for fixture 1081423 confirmed against the live fixtures API snapshot in data/node/raw/hotspawn_lol_fixtures.json (fetched 2026-10-24T15:34:30Z); page clock is US Eastern, 04:00 on 11.11.2026 == 09:00Z (EST, UTC-5)

flags.item: The published list was missing 20 live Hotspawn fixtures because refresh-picks failed four scheduled runs in a row
flags.detail: The canonical dataset was frozen at 2026-10-23T17:11:12Z while Hotspawn had already rotated its scheduled list. Comparing the published rows with the fixtures API snapshot the secondary pipeline fetched on 2026-10-24T15:34:30Z: 20 fixtures on the live feed are absent from the published site - all eight Worlds 2026 Main Event cards for 2026-10-24/25, four 4 Nations 2026 Halloween Heist cards, three Komplettligaen 2026 Autumn Playoffs cards, four Logitech G SuperStrike Cup Qualifier cards and one RIVALS LEAGUE Season 2 card - and 20 published rows had already been played and left the feed. Cause: the publish gate 'external receipts validated against the dataset' treated a book receipt whose fixture had simply been played as a hard failure, so committing any receipt guaranteed a self-inflicted outage within about a day. Failed runs: 40026767003, 40063260000, 40088464687, 40109474033. Fixed on branch arena/62ba9cfe-lolhotspawn1: such receipts are now retired rather than rejected, and corroboration-only checks are advisory, so they can never stop a data refresh again. The list below is the set of fixtures that were missing at the time this was written; it will be empty on the first successful refresh after the merge.
flags.verification: independent cross-pipeline comparison, 2026-10-24: canonical data/matches.json (inventory 2026-10-23T17:11:12Z, 241 rows) vs data/node/raw/hotspawn_lol_fixtures.json (fetched 2026-10-24T15:34:30Z, 241 scheduled of 1540 total). The eight Worlds kick-off times were separately confirmed against bo3.gg and EGamersWorld, which list the same eight cards on 2026-10-24 at the same US Eastern times.

flags.item: The 'displayed clock is UTC-4' note for bo3.gg and EGamersWorld is only correct until 2026-11-01
flags.detail: data/corroboration.json records both aggregators as 'Displayed clock is UTC-4 (US Eastern)'. Both actually display US Eastern local time, which is UTC-4 during EDT and UTC-5 during EST. US daylight saving ends on 2026-11-01, so from that date the same note is off by an hour and any receipt mapped with it lands on the wrong fixture. Verified both ways: 13:00 on 24.10.2026 (EDT) == 17:00Z, matching fixture 1067688; 00:00 on 10.11.2026 (EST) == 05:00Z, matching fixture 1081421; 04:00 on 11.11.2026 (EST) == 09:00Z, matching fixture 1081423. The correction is written into the receipt file header and into research/LONGTAIL_VENUES.md; the wording in data/corroboration.json is generated by tools/corroborate.py and is corrected there.
flags.verification: three independent fixture/page time pairs reconciled against the Hotspawn fixtures API on 2026-10-24; DST end date 2026-11-01 is the US federal rule (first Sunday in November)
